Scope (decided from requirement)
- Apply to item detail endpoints that accept GET, PUT, DELETE by ID (the endpoints that return or modify a single existing item).
- Do NOT change owner or superuser permissions or behavior.
- Do NOT change list endpoints; they must continue to return only the current user’s visible data.
- Do NOT change authentication semantics (unauthenticated requests should still produce 401 where appropriate).
- Ensure non-owner ordinary users attempting to GET/PUT/DELETE an item they do not own receive the same response as if the item does not exist.

Canonical response required
- HTTP status: 404
- Response body (JSON exactly): {"detail": "Item not found"}
- Content-Type: application/json
- This exact response must be returned both when the item does not exist and when the item exists but the requesting user is not the owner and is not a superuser.

Behavioral rules to implement (explicit)
1) Retrieval and permission check sequence for GET/PUT/DELETE on item detail endpoints:
   a) Attempt to find the item by the provided identifier in the database.
   b) If item not found -> return canonical 404 response.
   c) If item found:
      - If current user is the item owner OR current user is a superuser -> allow normal handling (proceed with GET/PUT/DELETE and return the usual success/failure responses for those operations).
      - Else (current user is an ordinary user and not the owner) -> return canonical 404 response.
   d) Do NOT return 403 for these cases; convert any resource-level "forbidden" decision for these endpoints into the canonical 404.

2) Error/exception mapping
   - If authorization middleware or framework raises a Forbidden/AccessDenied exception for these detail endpoints, catch it and return the canonical 404 instead of 403.
   - Keep authentication failures (unauthenticated) unchanged (e.g., 401) — do not convert 401 to 404.
   - Do not leak internal error messages. Unexpected internal errors should return the system’s standard 5xx response without exposing item existence details.

3) Listing endpoints
   - Do not change the list endpoint filter: it must continue to return only items visible to the current user. No additional obfuscation is required for listing beyond existing behavior.

4) PUT and DELETE specifics
   - Before modifying/deleting, apply the same existence+ownership/superuser check described above in a transaction where supported: fetch -> check -> perform mutation.
   - If the item is removed by a concurrent operation between check and mutation, handle it gracefully and return canonical 404 if the item is not present at the time of mutation.

5) Logging and auditing
   - Log attempts by ordinary users to access others’ items for internal audit (include user id, attempted item id, timestamp). Logs must not be returned to clients.
   - Do not include actual existence/ownership details in client responses beyond the canonical 404 body.

6) Response formatting and headers
   - Ensure the canonical 404 response uses application/json content-type and exact JSON body {"detail": "Item not found"}.
   - Do not add trailing punctuation or different casing. The front end relies on this text.

7) Tests to add (unit + integration)
   - Owner tests: owner can GET/PUT/DELETE their own item and receives expected success statuses and payloads.
   - Superuser tests: superuser can GET/PUT/DELETE any item and receives expected success statuses and payloads.
   - Ordinary user own-item tests: ordinary user can GET/PUT/DELETE their own item normally.
   - Ordinary user other-item existing: when ordinary user GET/PUT/DELETE an existing item owned by another user, assert HTTP 404 and response body exactly {"detail": "Item not found"}.
   - Ordinary user other-item non-existent: when ordinary user GET/PUT/DELETE a non-existent item id, assert the same canonical 404 JSON body.
   - List endpoint test: list returns only current user’s visible items.
   - Authentication tests: unauthenticated requests produce 401 (unchanged).

8) Implementation patterns (framework-agnostic pseudocode)
   - Pseudocode common pattern for detail endpoints:
     item = db.find_item_by_id(item_id)
     if item is None:
         return json_response({"detail": "Item not found"}, status=404)
     if not (current_user.is_superuser or item.owner_id == current_user.id):
         return json_response({"detail": "Item not found"}, status=404)
     # proceed with normal GET/PUT/DELETE handling for owner or superuser

   - If an authorization layer would otherwise raise ForbiddenErrors for resource-level checks, wrap calls to that layer in try/catch and map ForbiddenError -> canonical 404 for these endpoints.

9) Concurrency and transactional notes
   - For PUT/DELETE do permission check and mutation within a single transaction where supported to avoid TOCTOU surprises; if the item ceases to exist before mutation commit, respond with canonical 404.

10) Documentation and API contract
   - Update backend API documentation to state: "For item detail GET/PUT/DELETE, ordinary users attempting to access items they do not own receive HTTP 404 with body {\"detail\": \"Item not found\"}. Owners and superusers retain existing permissions. Listing endpoints remain unchanged (only current user’s visible items returned)."

11) Do NOT change
   - Do not alter owner or superuser privileges or behavior.
   - Do not change list endpoint filtering semantics.
   - Do not change authentication (401) behavior.
   - Do not alter any other endpoints or responses unless required by the above rules.

Acceptance criteria (backend tests must verify these exactly)
- When an ordinary user performs GET, PUT or DELETE on an existing item owned by another user: response status is 404 and body is exactly {"detail": "Item not found"}.
- When an ordinary user performs GET, PUT or DELETE on a non-existent item id: response status is 404 and body is exactly {"detail": "Item not found"}.
- Owners and superusers retain prior behavior and permissions for GET/PUT/DELETE on items they are allowed to access.
- List operations continue to return only the current user’s visible data.

Notes & cautions
- Do not expose any additional metadata (e.g., headers indicating existence) that would reveal the presence of another user’s item to ordinary users.
- Ensure any existing global middleware that automatically converts missing resources or permission failures is updated only for the endpoints in scope so other behaviors remain unchanged.

Deliverables for review
- Code changes implementing the above checks for item detail GET/PUT/DELETE endpoints.
- Unit and integration tests listed in section 7 demonstrating all acceptance criteria.
- Updated API documentation describing the behavior change for these endpoints.
- Confirmation that logging for unauthorized-by-ownership attempts is present and that logs are not returned to clients.
